_doc: Address and concept pairs with the pathway the Planning Code gives, each with the code text it rests on. tests/test_pathway_cases.py builds the zoning and overlay rows for each case from the rule table the product uses (precedent/static/sf_overlay_rules.json through the datasf_zoning, datasf_sud and static_rules sources and the file-backed store), runs app.memo.pathway.determine (rule table v2, rules in force on 2026-11-10) and compares. Each case is run twice: as its profile is written here, and stated in full (the test supplies the inputs rule table v2 reads and the profile does not carry). scripts/validation/check_pathway_cases.py runs the same cases, as written, against the local validation database.
_source_note: Code text read on 2026-11-10 from the gocodebook.com mirror (San Francisco Planning Code, 2026-08 edition, text as of 2026-09-23). codelibrary.amlegal.com refused automated access (HTTP 403), so no quote comes from the official copy. Table rows are quoted with ' | ' between cells. 'source' is the first reader's findings; 'reread_2026_11_10' holds the passages read again while reconciling; 'second_reading' sums up a blind second reading and keeps what it read outside the mirror.

_fields.expected: What the rules must return for the concept AS WRITTEN (the profile below, unchanged since rule table v1): use, permission for a new use of that kind, existing use, change of use and each row's status. Rule table v2 reads inputs the profile does not carry (how the licence is to be obtained, whether the business is part of a chain, the floor area, the closing hour, whether an existing business changes). A row that needs one of them is 'insufficient_information' and names it; a control that cannot be decided without one reads permission 'not_covered'. A missing input is never filled with an assumption. null for a disputed case.
_fields.expected_missing_inputs: For each row that is insufficient_information as written: the inputs it names, in the rules' fixed phrases.
_fields.expected_note: Why 'expected' differs from 'code_answer': which input the concept text does not give, or which fact the rules cannot place.
_fields.code_answer: The Planning Code's answer (for a depends_on_fact case, the best case), as the readers took the concept: what the rules must return once the inputs are given (tests/test_pathway_cases.py, stated_in_full). This is the answer this file held as 'expected' under rule table v1. null for a disputed case.
_fields.disputed: true: the readings could not be settled. The case is left out of the pass or fail assertions and listed. 'dispute.rules_read' pins what the rules return, without calling either reading right.
_fields.rules_gap: Set when the rules cannot return the right answer. 'rules_return' is what they return as written (with the inputs their rows name in 'rules_return_missing_inputs'), 'rules_return_stated_in_full' what they return once the inputs are given.
_fields.rules_gap_closed: Set when rule table v2 closed a gap of rule table v1: 'was' keeps the old entry, 'closed_by' says what closed it.
_fields.depends_on_fact: Set when the Code's answer turns on a fact that is not on file. 'code_answer' is then the answer if the fact goes the applicant's way (the best case), which is what the rules return; 'otherwise' is the Code's answer if it does not. Left out of the undisputed count. Where the rules name the fact instead of returning the best case, 'rules_return_stated_in_full' is what they return stated in full and 'rules_name' the phrase they name it with.
_fields.store.overlays[].rule_table_now: Fields where the corrected rule table differs from the row as recorded.
_fields.licences[].at_address: false: a licence near the address or on its parcel that must not be read as this address.

As written the row cannot be decided without: how the liquor licence will be obtained (new, or a transfer from another owner or another location). It is insufficient information and names them. source.quote: any permitted conditional use may continue in the form in which it was authorized, or in the form in which it lawfully existed either on the effective date of this Code or the effective date of any amendment imposing new conditional use requirements upon such use or feature
source.reading: An existing lawful bar may continue as a bar without a new Conditional Use; this is the Code basis for rule Z1 (allowed, the use already exists).

source.quote: A permitted conditional use that is discontinued for a period of three years, or otherwise abandoned, shall not be restored, except upon approval of a new conditional use application pursuant to the provisions of Article 3 of this Code.
source.reading: The 'already exists' answer holds only while the bar use has not lapsed for three years; an ACTIVE licence is the evidence the rules use for that.

source.quote: (1) A permitted conditional use may not be significantly altered, enlarged, or intensified, except upon approval of a new conditional use application pursuant to the provisions of Article 3 of this Code.
source.reading: If the new operator enlarges or intensifies the bar, a new Conditional Use is needed even with no change of use.

source.quote: Bar. A Retail Sales and Service Use that provides on-site alcoholic beverage sales for drinking on the premises, including bars serving beer, wine, and/or liquor to the customer where no person under 21 years of age is admitted (with Alcoholic Beverage Control [ABC] license types 23, 42, 48, or 61)
source.reading: A Type 48 premises is a Bar under § 102, so the licence on file shows an existing Bar and the proposed use is the same.

conditions_the_rules_cannot_evaluate: Whether the bar use was lawfully established and has not been discontinued for three years or abandoned (§ 178(a), (d)). The rules take the ACTIVE Type 48 licence as the evidence.
Whether the new operator significantly alters, enlarges or intensifies the use (§ 178(c)(1)); that would need a new Conditional Use even though the use does not change.
Whether the licence on file passes to the new operator at the same premises. A new or relocated bar must instead use a licence transferred from another bar inside the Mission SUD (§ 249.60(b)(2)(C)).
Story: Bar is C on the first story only (Table 762).

§ 249.60(b)(2)(C) limits the licence of a new or relocated Bar. The rules do not apply it when the records show the same use already in place (rule A2 is skipped when change of use is no), so the alcohol row is further review (rule A3).

Address matching: active eating-place licences sit within 8 metres at other addresses (abc:678716, Type 41, 538 Valencia St; abc:506818, Type 47, 546 Valencia St). They must not count. If they did, rule 3 would see both kinds and return not established.
Older planning records on the same parcel are filed under 542 Valencia St (for example datasf_planning:2003.0868C, 'To add a place of entertainment to the existing bar'). They do not affect rule 3.
